title: The yawn you caught while reading this
text: Yawning is {{1}} contagious {{2}} merely reading about it can set one off. Scientists still debate {{3}} we yawn at all, though the leading idea is that a yawn cools the brain, and a stuffy room or a long meeting certainly helps one along. Watching somebody yawn is not even necessary: hearing a yawn, or reading about one, works {{4}} well. {{5}} is less clear is {{6}} contagion works — stretching and laughing spread in company too — but studies suggest {{7}} with more empathetic personalities catch yawns more readily, and so, curiously, do dogs. {{8}} remains possible that the yawn is society's oldest synchronising signal: one person's drowsiness, broadcast to the group, gently reminds everyone that it might be time to rest.
